15.1: The image of the eternal ashvattha tree with roots above and branches below, whose leaves are the Vedic hymns — knowing it, one knows the Vedas.
15.2: Its branches spread below and above, nourished by the gunas; its roots stretch downward as actions in the world of men.
15.3: Its form is not perceived here, nor its end, beginning or foundation; cut this firm-rooted tree with the strong axe of non-attachment.
15.4: Then seek that goal from which, once reached, none return, taking refuge in the primal Person from whom this ancient current came forth.
15.5: Free from pride and delusion, conquering attachment, ever dwelling in the Self, desire gone, released from the pairs of pleasure and pain, they reach that eternal goal.
15.6: Neither the sun nor the moon nor fire illumines that abode; going there, none return — that is My supreme abode.
15.7: An eternal fragment of Myself, becoming a living soul in the world, draws to itself the senses and the mind that rest in nature.
15.8: When the lord of the body takes up a body or leaves it, he carries these with him as the wind carries scents from their source.
15.9: Presiding over hearing, sight, touch, taste, smell and the mind, he experiences the objects of the senses.
15.10: The deluded do not see him departing or dwelling or experiencing; those with the eye of knowledge see.
15.11: Yogis striving see Him seated in themselves; the unrefined, however much they strive, do not.
15.12: The light in the sun that illumines the whole world, and the light in the moon and in fire — know that light to be Mine.
15.13: Entering the earth, I support all beings with My energy; becoming the sap-giving moon, I nourish all plants.
15.14: Becoming the fire of digestion in the bodies of living beings, joined with the two breaths, I digest the four kinds of food.
15.15: I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me come memory, knowledge and their loss; I alone am to be known by all the Vedas.
15.16: There are two persons in the world, the perishable and the imperishable: all beings are perishable, the unchanging is imperishable.
15.17: But the highest Person is another — called the supreme Self, the eternal Lord who enters the three worlds and sustains them.
15.18: Because I transcend the perishable and am higher even than the imperishable, I am known in the world and in the Vedas as the supreme Person.
15.19: One who, undeluded, knows Me as the supreme Person knows all and worships Me with the whole being.
15.20: Thus the most secret teaching has been declared; knowing it, one becomes wise and all duties are fulfilled.
